newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai aims to reform rural credit cooperatives.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai aims to reform rural credit cooperatives.

text.p: Shanghai, China's financial capital, has launched an effort to standardise and reform its rural credit cooperatives in a bid to eventually transform them into cooperative banks, the Xinhua news agency said on Tuesday.
Shanghai has 227 rural credit cooperatives, a type of non-banking financial institution that pools credit at the local level, which were set up in the 1950s, the report said.
The city's first standardised rural credit cooperative, the Shiwan Rural Credit Cooperative, officially began operations last Friday, it said, but gave no further details.
The city also aims to convert credit cooperatives in urban areas into cooperative banks as part of reforms to the banking system, the agency said, quoting a Shanghai official.
